title: The Fountys
subtitle: Art History Awards Show
challenge: Space One Eleven is a visual arts gallery and non-profit that needed a creative fundraising event to match the tone of the organization.
project: We produced, wrote, and emceed an art history awards show featuring some of the city's most beloved artists. Each local artist was cast as an iconic figure from art history, and presented or accepted an award in character. Winners of each category were determined by an online vote.
Inspired by Marcel Duchamp's infamous 1917 masterpiece "Fountain" (the urinal), small golden ceramic replicas ("Fountys") were presented to the winners in 12 categories.
highlights: Most Whimsical Representation of the Human Body: Pablo Picasso
Most Posthumous Success: Vincent Van Gogh

title: Recycled Runway
subtitle: A New Signature Event
challenge: The Bib & Tucker Sew Op needed a new fundraising event that engaged the public and illustrated the impact of their mission of "building community through education, economic opportunity, and sustainable practices, using the art of sewing." Over three years, Recycled Runway became a favorite event for supporters of Birmingham's textile community.
project: We created, organized, marketed, and emceed an event that highlighted the work of local seamstresses. Teams signed up and were assigned a seamstress and a model. Each team was provided with a mystery box of garments and had 90 minutes to sew together a custom outfit, culminating in a runway fashion show judged by local style influencers.

title: Why'd They Do That?!
subtitle: A Game Show About Life and Politics in Alabama
project: "Why'd They Do That?!" a Game Show About Life and Politics in Alabama was a romp through the quizzical, nonsensical, and downright ridiculous moments in the annals of Alabama that make us all ask ourselves "why'd they do that?!" - all to help energize voters ahead of critical midterm elections across the state.
Members of local Democratic organizations, elected officials, and comedians competed in this uproarious game show, scoring points for both creativity and correct answers.

title: Can You Repeat That?
subtitle: A Game Show About the Magic City
challenge: The Birmingham History Center wanted to bring energy and humor to a fundraising event to raise awareness and support for its mission of preserving the artifacts and stories from the Magic City's fascinating past.
project: We wrote, produced, and emceed a sold-out game show about The Magic City called "Can You Repeat That?" at the historic Virginia Samford Theater, featuring local luminaries like James Spann, Frank Stitt, former mayor Richard Arrington Jr, and then mayor William Bell.

title: The Other Awards
subtitle: Celebrating Unsung Heroes
challenge: Too often, awards ceremonies honor prominent and successful local leaders, while those who contribute to the charm and heartbeat of a community go unrecognized.
project: We wrote, produced, and emceed the Other Awards to celebrate unsung heroes in the Birmingham community in categories like: "Best Birmingham City School Teacher", "Most Passionate Neighborhood Association Attendee", "Best Service Industry Worker", and more.

title: Romantically Challenged
project: For seven years, Romantically Challenged was Birmingham’s most enchanting and rambunctious dating game show. In an era where apps dominated the dating landscape, the event provided a welcome respite from swiping fatigue.

Hundreds of people applied each year to be contestants, and the ones selected to be on the show answered a variety of questions and performed a host of silly challenges to win the hearts of featured bachelors and bachelorettes. Along with Max, the event was co-hosted by two of Birmingham’s favorite drag queens, Sharon Cocx and Reese Eve Cocx.
Over the years, proceeds from the event benefited a number of organizations, including Equality Alabama and the Crisis Center.
